result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.neighbors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get neighbors of a node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4918-L5015){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.neighbors( node, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Ego network](/assets/graphs/algo-ego-network.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node graph centered on an ego node. The ego and its three neighbors, along with all edges among them, are shown in the accent color. A fifth node lies outside the ego network; the edge that reaches it from one of the neighbors is drawn in default styling to mark the boundary." width="100%"} Returns the neighboring nodes of a specified node, with control over directionality (for directed graphs). For directed graphs, the default mode is `"out"` (outgoing neighbors only). For undirected graphs, mode doesn't affect the result since all edges are bidirectional. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node ID or label to find neighbors for. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Direction mode for neighbor lookup: (1) `"out"`, only successors (outgoing edges) which is the default for directed graphs, (2) `"in"`, only predecessors (incoming edges), and (3) `"all"`, both successors and predecessors. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of neighbor node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `mode=` is not one of `"out"`, `"in"`, or `"all"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} By default, `mode="out"` returns only outgoing neighbors -- here node "A"'s only outgoing edge points to "B": ::: {#3e45d7bb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node("A") graph.add_node("B") graph.add_node("C") graph.add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.0) graph.add_edge("C", "A", weight=2.0) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") out_neighbors = graph.neighbors(a_id, mode="out") out_neighbors ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [2] ``` ::: ::: `mode="in"` instead follows incoming edges -- "C" points to "A", so it's the only predecessor: ::: {#f86420aa .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.neighbors(a_id, mode="in") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [3] ``` ::: ::: `mode="all"` combines both directions: ::: {#5509be0e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.neighbors(a_id, mode="all") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [2, 3] ``` ::: ::: Since results are node IDs rather than labels, map them back with `get_label_from_id()` when a human-readable answer is needed: ::: {#afa95832 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in out_neighbors] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: :::
